chapter_title: Concerning the Seven Works of the Living Spirit
chapter_note: The chapter is dominated by a compact, enumerated cosmological teaching: a seven-fold list of the Living Spirit’s works (plus a final eschatological addition). The only clear editorial frame is the dialogue-attribution in ¶1 and a beatitude-style closing in ¶10. No NT citation formulas appear; most content stays cosmos→cosmos (beings, zones, vessels, powers).

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit has done seven [wo]rks with his strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "[Once] again the enlightener speaks:" (late compiling voice; not part of the impersonal teaching).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerated cosmological topic-statement is core in structure, but the speech-attribution to "the enlightener" is a later hagiographic/dialogue frame marker that must be stripped.

paragraphs.core_text: [The fi]rst: He brought the First Man up from the contest, the way a pearl is [brought] up from the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic actor (Living Spirit) → cosmic rescue of First Man, expressed through a correspondential simile (pearl/sea) that remains within the system (redeemed light extracted from mixture). Impersonal enumerated-list style.

paragraphs.core_text: [The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified [h]im in every body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still cosmos→cosmos: a rebel/demonic figure is bound/distributed through bodies. The verb "crucified" may be later Christianized diction, but there is no NT entry-vector (no citation/narrative); the sentence functions as a cosmological mechanism within the seven-works list.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: He [tr]ampled, piled up, and pierced the essences of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanical, violent verbs describing subjugation of Death-powers; fits the impersonal action-catalogue of cosmic construction/defeat.

paragraphs.core_text: [The f]ourth: He constructed the ships of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct cosmological construction statement (ships of light) within the enumerated work-list; no audience address or institutional reach.

paragraphs.core_text: The fi[f]th: He evoked his five sons, and distributed them about. They [took] possession of the zone, they bore up under all the universe's weight. Also, he evoked three living words. He set [them] upon the th[re]e vessels, another one upon the giant. [Again, he evoked the] summons, that it might be mixed with the five shining men.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly diagnostic of the substrate: numbered structuring (five sons; three living words; three vessels), cosmic geography (zone), and functional placement (bearing the universe’s weight). The whole paragraph stays within cosmic architecture and degree-mappings.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.86⟩ The sixth: When he had constructed the zone he aro[se] and s[e]nt forth a multitude of powers and many [angel]s; so that they would bound the circuit of the z[o]ne on every si[de], un[t]il he finished [co]nstructing the works. And at the end [of] all the [wor]ks he to[ok s]ome of them into his storehouses, and he appointed others at the watch-posts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-building logistics (bounding the zone, storehouses, watch-posts) expressed in impersonal expository narrative; still cosmos→cosmos without polemical or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The [sev]enth: A[t the] time when the Ambass[ador dis]pl[aye]d his glorious imag[e], the L[iving] Spirit [established] many [go]ds and angels. They [ ... ] Th[ey to]ok hold of it, that the entire building [ ... ] not [ ... / ... ] one another against [the] light, which he had [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-hierarchical scene (Ambassador’s image; establishment of gods/angels) tied to stabilizing the cosmic building; remains internal to the system despite lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: Also another gr[ea]t and glorious work he will enact at the e[nd] is [the] Last [Statue], which he will bring up to the aeons of [light]; and he [ ... ] in, and [he ta]kes hold, and he smites [ ... ], and [he] builds, and he [ ... ], and he [ ... t]hem.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological-cosmological mechanism (Last Statue; ascent to aeons of Light) remains cosmos→cosmos. The phrase "Also another" after the sevenfold list may signal secondary expansion, but it is not an institutional seam and contains no NT entry-vector.

Beatitude-style closure ("Blessed is he...") functions as an editorial/performative ending rather than part of the impersonal seven-works cosmological catalogue; no additional cosmological mapping is introduced.
